statements.label: supported
statements.text: When an adenosine carries the m6A mark, the surrounding RNA sequence becomes more accessible for binding by HNRNPG.
statements.evidence: Here, we show that m6A increases the accessibility of its surrounding RNA sequence to bind heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein G (HNRNPG).
statements.note: The abstract states that m6A increases the accessibility of the surrounding RNA sequence to HNRNPG binding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study identified 13,191 m6A sites across the transcriptome that modulate RNA-HNRNPG interaction, thereby changing expression and alternative splicing of target mRNAs.
statements.evidence: We identified 13,191 m6A sites in the transcriptome that regulate RNA-HNRNPG interaction and thereby alter the expression and alternative splicing pattern of target mRNAs.
statements.note: The abstract reports 13,191 m6A sites that regulate RNA-HNRNPG interaction and alter the expression and splicing of target mRNAs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The C-terminal low-complexity region of HNRNPG self-assembles into large particles inside living cells.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, HNRNPG binds m6A-methylated RNAs through its C-terminal low-complexity region, which self-assembles into large particles in vitro.
statements.note: The abstract reports particle self-assembly only in vitro and says nothing about whether the region forms particles in cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: HNRNPG needs the Arg-Gly-Gly repeats in its low-complexity region to bind the RNA motif that m6A methylation exposes.
statements.evidence: The Arg-Gly-Gly repeats within the low-complexity region are required for binding to the RNA motif exposed by m6A methylation.
statements.note: The abstract states that these Arg-Gly-Gly repeats are required for binding the motif exposed by m6A methylation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: High circNRIP1 expression in gastric tumours is associated with shorter overall survival of gastric cancer patients.
statements.evidence: We proved that circNRIP1 sponges miR-149-5p to affect the expression level of AKT1 and eventually acts as a tumour promotor in GC.
statements.note: The abstract establishes circNRIP1 as a tumour promotor in cells, mice and PDX models but reports no patient survival or prognosis data.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In RNA-seq data, circNRIP1 was found at higher levels in gastric cancer.
statements.evidence: We detected higher circNRIP1 expression in gastric cancer by performing RNA-seq analysis.
statements.note: The abstract states that RNA-seq analysis detected higher circNRIP1 expression in gastric cancer.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking down circNRIP1 in gastric cancer cells blocked their proliferation, migration and invasion and lowered AKT1 expression.
statements.evidence: We discovered that knockdown of circNRIP1 successfully blocked proliferation, migration, invasion and the expression level of AKT1 in GC cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports that circNRIP1 knockdown blocked proliferation, migration, invasion and AKT1 expression in GC cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gastric cancer cells can pass circNRIP1 to one another through exosomes, and exosomal circNRIP1 promoted tumour metastasis in vivo.
statements.evidence: Moreover, it was proven that circNRIP1 can be transmitted by exosomal communication between GC cells, and exosomal circNRIP1 promoted tumour metastasis in vivo.
statements.note: The abstract states that circNRIP1 is transmitted between GC cells by exosomes and that exosomal circNRIP1 promoted metastasis in vivo.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing DWORF in mouse cardiomyocytes raised peak Ca2+ transient amplitude and SR Ca2+ load and shortened the time constant of cytosolic Ca2+ decay.
statements.evidence: In mice, overexpression of DWORF in cardiomyocytes increases peak Ca(2+) transient amplitude and SR Ca(2+) load while reducing the time constant of cytosolic Ca(2+) decay during each cycle of contraction-relaxation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that DWORF overexpression in mouse cardiomyocytes increases peak Ca2+ transients and SR Ca2+ load while reducing the Ca2+ decay time constant.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A putative muscle-specific long noncoding RNA turned out to encode a 34-amino-acid peptide, which was named DWORF.
statements.evidence: We discovered a putative muscle-specific long noncoding RNA that encodes a peptide of 34 amino acids and that we named dwarf open reading frame (DWORF).
statements.note: The abstract states that the putative muscle-specific lncRNA encodes a 34-amino-acid peptide named DWORF.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Slow skeletal muscle without DWORF shows lower SERCA activity and slower Ca2+ clearance and relaxation.
statements.evidence: Conversely, slow skeletal muscle lacking DWORF exhibits delayed Ca(2+) clearance and relaxation and reduced SERCA activity.
statements.note: The abstract reports delayed Ca2+ clearance and relaxation and reduced SERCA activity in slow skeletal muscle lacking DWORF.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: DWORF expression is reduced in the hearts of human patients with heart failure.
statements.evidence: DWORF is the only endogenous peptide known to activate the SERCA pump by physical interaction and provides a means for enhancing muscle contractility.
statements.note: The abstract describes DWORF function in mouse muscle and does not report DWORF levels in human hearts or in heart failure.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: By disrupting the interaction between PHD2 and HIF-1α, HISLA protects HIF-1α from hydroxylation and degradation.
statements.evidence: Mechanistically, HISLA blocks the interaction of PHD2 and HIF-1α to inhibit the hydroxylation and degradation of HIF-1α.
statements.note: The abstract states that HISLA blocks the PHD2-HIF-1α interaction and thereby inhibits HIF-1α hydroxylation and degradation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Blocking EV-transmitted HISLA reduces breast cancer metastasis in mice.
statements.evidence: Blocking EV-transmitted HISLA inhibits the glycolysis and chemoresistance of breast cancer in vivo.
statements.note: The in vivo effects of blocking HISLA reported in the abstract are on glycolysis and chemoresistance; metastasis is never mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In breast cancer patients, shorter survival and poor chemotherapeutic response went together with HISLA expression in tumour-associated macrophages.
statements.evidence: Clinically, HISLA expression in TAMs is associated with glycolysis, poor chemotherapeutic response and shorter survival of patients with breast cancer.
statements.note: The abstract states that HISLA expression in TAMs is associated with poor chemotherapeutic response and shorter survival in breast cancer patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Lactate released by glycolytic tumour cells increases HISLA levels in macrophages, creating a feed-forward loop between the two cell types.
statements.evidence: Reciprocally, lactate released from glycolytic tumour cells upregulates HISLA in macrophages, constituting a feed-forward loop between TAMs and tumour cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports that tumour-derived lactate upregulates HISLA in macrophages, forming a feed-forward loop between TAMs and tumour cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Intestinal epithelial cells and Hopx-positive cells are the main cellular sources of the miRNAs found in feces.
statements.evidence: Cell-specific loss of the miRNA-processing enzyme, Dicer, identified intestinal epithelial cells (IEC) and Hopx-positive cells as predominant fecal miRNA sources.
statements.note: The abstract states that cell-specific Dicer deletion identified IEC and Hopx-positive cells as the predominant fecal miRNA sources.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mice lacking Dicer1 in intestinal epithelial cells develop more severe colitis and an uncontrolled gut microbiota.
statements.evidence: IEC-miRNA-deficient (Dicer1(ΔIEC)) mice exhibit uncontrolled gut microbiota and exacerbated colitis
statements.note: The abstract reports that IEC-miRNA-deficient Dicer1(ΔIEC) mice show uncontrolled gut microbiota and exacerbated colitis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Transplanting fecal miRNA from healthy donors relieves colitis in human patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
statements.evidence: These findings identify both a physiologic role by which fecal miRNA shapes the gut microbiota and a potential strategy for manipulating the microbiome.
statements.note: The abstract reports colitis relief from fecal miRNA transplantation only in mice and calls microbiome manipulation merely a potential strategy, with no human data.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Fecal miRNAs enter bacteria such as F. nucleatum and E. coli, where they specifically regulate bacterial gene transcripts and alter bacterial growth.
statements.evidence: These miRNAs can enter bacteria, such as F. nucleatum and E. coli, specifically regulate bacterial gene transcripts, and affect bacterial growth.
statements.note: The abstract states that these fecal miRNAs can enter bacteria such as F. nucleatum and E. coli, regulate their transcripts and affect their growth.
